subject.title: Carry provider-authoritative agent identity for adopted catalog sessions

question: Should catalog continuation require providers to return the authoritative owning `agentId` now, or should this contract change wait until non-default-agent adoption is introduced?
rationale: The invariant is valid, but changing the provider result affects a plugin-facing ownership contract while the failure mode is not currently reachable; repository policy requires an explicit compatibility and timing choice.

options.title: Add authoritative identity now
options.body: Add the provider-owned agent ID across bundled adapters, gateway handling, upstream-link storage, and multi-agent regression tests before non-default adoption makes the latent ambiguity reachable.

options.title: Defer with the adoption feature
options.body: Keep this issue as the prerequisite for any future non-default-agent adoption and implement both changes together when that capability is sponsored.

options.title: Introduce a compatibility transition
options.body: Add an optional provider field with a named deprecation plan for key-derived ownership, then make authoritative identity mandatory after external providers have migrated.

recommendation.title: Add authoritative identity now
recommendation.body: Add the provider-owned agent ID across bundled adapters, gateway handling, upstream-link storage, and multi-agent regression tests before non-default adoption makes the latent ambiguity reachable.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged feature history shows direct ownership of both catalog continuation and adopted-session upstream monitoring.
